\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حکمران} (hukmrān)}{حکمران (hukmrān)}]{\ur{حکمران} (hukmrān) — a ruler}

\label{lesson:UR-C341-hukmran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an arbiter, then the Urdu for to testify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حکمران}}
\textbf{\ur{حکمران}} — \emph{hukmrān} — \textquotedblleft{}a ruler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{ملک} \ur{کا} \ur{حکمران} \ur{بادشاہ} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is mulk kā hukmrān bādshāh thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The ruler of this country was a king.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حکمران}} (\emph{hukmrān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hukmrān}: Arabic \emph{ḥukm}, \textquotedblleft{}an order\textquotedblright{}, with Persian \emph{-rān}, \textquotedblleft{}driving\textquotedblright{}. One who runs the orders.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hukmrān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hukmrān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is mulk kā hukmrān bādshāh thā.} — The ruler of this country was a king.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an arbiter, then the Urdu for to testify, then say \emph{hukmrān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{حکمران} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A ruler\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پالیسی} (pālīsī)}{پالیسی (pālīsī)}]{\ur{پالیسی} (pālīsī) — a policy}

\label{lesson:UR-C341-palisi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to testify, then the Urdu for a ruler.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پالیسی}}
\textbf{\ur{پالیسی}} — \emph{pālīsī} — \textquotedblleft{}a policy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{حکومت} \ur{کی} \ur{نئی} \ur{پالیسی} \ur{کیا} \ur{ہے؟}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hukūmat kī naī pālīsī kyā hai?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What is the government's new policy?
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پالیسی}} (\emph{pālīsī}) is borrowed from English \emph{policy}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تجویز} (tajvīz)}{تجویز (tajvīz)}]{\ur{تجویز} (tajvīz) — a proposal; a suggestion}

\label{lesson:UR-C341-tajviz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a ruler, then the Urdu for a policy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تجویز}}
\textbf{\ur{تجویز}} — \emph{tajvīz} — \textquotedblleft{}a proposal; a suggestion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وزیر} \ur{نے} \ur{ایک} \ur{نئی} \ur{تجویز} \ur{دی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vazīr ne ek naī tajvīz dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister put forward a new proposal.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تجویز}} (\emph{tajvīz}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tajwīz}, \textquotedblleft{}allowing, approving\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for a proposal put forward for others to approve, a sense our sources do not trace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a ruler, then the Urdu for a policy, then say \emph{tajvīz} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اقتدار} (iqtidār)}{اقتدار (iqtidār)}]{\ur{اقتدار} (iqtidār) — the power to rule}

\label{lesson:UR-C341-iqtidar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a policy, then the Urdu for a proposal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اقتدار}}
\textbf{\ur{اقتدار}} — \emph{iqtidār} — \textquotedblleft{}the power to rule\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{دس} \ur{سال} \ur{اقتدار} \ur{میں} \ur{رہا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh das sāl iqtidār meṅ rahā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He was in power for ten years.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اقتدار}} (\emph{iqtidār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iqtidār}, \textquotedblleft{}being able; power\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹھہرانا} (ṭhahrānā)}{ٹھہرانا (ṭhahrānā)}]{\ur{ٹھہرانا} (ṭhahrānā) — to hold to be; to declare (guilty)}

\label{lesson:UR-C341-thahrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a proposal, then the Urdu for the power to rule.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹھہرانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھہرانا}} — \emph{ṭhahrānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold to be; to declare (guilty)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوگوں} \ur{نے} \ur{حکومت} \ur{کو} \ur{ذمہ} \ur{دار} \ur{ٹھہرایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{logoṅ ne hukūmat ko zimme-dār ṭhahrāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People held the government responsible.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{ذمہ} \ur{دار} \ur{ٹھہرایا}, \emph{us ne mujhe zimme-dār ṭhahrāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھہرانا}} (\emph{ṭhahrānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{ٹھہرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop, to settle\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭhaharnā} under \emph{*stabhira}, \textquotedblleft{}fixed, firm\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13680). To make a verdict settle on someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhahrānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{logoṅ ne hukūmat ko zimme-dār ṭhahrāyā.} — People held the government responsible.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a proposal, then the Urdu for the power to rule, then say \emph{ṭhahrānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
